name: F-16C Block 50 (open-source data), fitted to DCS
description: F-16C with thrust x1.138, CD0 x2.927, K_IND x1.737, CL_MAX x0.883, DRAG_RISE_PEAK x0.300, g lag 1.00 s building up and 1.92 s coming off, fitted by dcs/stick/manoeuvre.py to the player's F-16C in DCS flown by the stick pilot. Record manoeuvre_20261014_104111.json; mismatch 5.135 -> 2.461.

sources.MASS_EMPTY: open-source F-16C Block 50 estimate (as calibrated in f16_sim.py)
sources.FUEL_FULL: open-source F-16C Block 50 estimate (as calibrated in f16_sim.py)
sources.CD0: x2.927 of the F-16C's 0.013: fitted by dcs/stick/manoeuvre.py --fit to manoeuvre_20261014_104111 (the player's F-16C in DCS, four AIM-120, flown by the stick pilot); checked on manoeuvre_20261014_112025 (mismatch 2.73, not fitted to it). High for an F-16: this loadout's drag in DCS, and it trades against DRAG_RISE_PEAK
sources.K_IND: x1.737 of the F-16C's 0.133: fitted by dcs/stick/manoeuvre.py --fit to manoeuvre_20261014_104111 (the player's F-16C in DCS, four AIM-120, flown by the stick pilot); checked on manoeuvre_20261014_112025 (mismatch 2.73, not fitted to it)
sources.CL_ALPHA: open-source F-16C Block 50 estimate (as calibrated in f16_sim.py)
sources.CL_MAX: measured, not fitted: the 90th percentile of CL = g x weight / (q x S_REF) with the stick at its stop above 2 g, 1.28 / 1.26 / 1.28 in three DCS flights (14 October); DCS's flight control limits the angle of attack
sources.CL_MIN: open-source F-16C Block 50 estimate (as calibrated in f16_sim.py)
sources.DRAG_RISE_M1: where the model's rise has always peaked; see Peak extra CD
sources.DRAG_RISE_M2: peak 0.034 at Mach 0.975, decay 0.7, wave drag held beyond Mach 1.4: top speed at full afterburner is Mach 1.24 at 500 m, 1.37 at 3 km, 1.66 at 9 km and the Mach 1.8 cap at 12 km (published: ≈ 1.2 low, ≈ 2 at altitude). History: the rise was a half sine that fell back to zero just below Mach 1.1 and jumped to the peak there (a low-drag gap across Mach 1.0–1.1); now a quarter sine to the same peak at 0.975, so the curve below 0.975 is unchanged and top speed moved only at 500 m (from Mach 1.17). Before that, peak 0.040, decay 2.0 and zero drag above Mach 1.4: Mach 1.8 even at sea level
